mainTopic: Righteous figures who 'did not sin': דוד and לשון הרע, שלמה, and יאשיהו
overview: This amud finishes the story of דוד, מפיבשת, and ציבא. The גמרא reads מפיבשת's reply as a hidden complaint against God for bringing דוד home safely, and it explains the name מריב בעל and the בת קול 'quarreler, son of a quarreler' in that light. רב teaches that because דוד split the field after accepting ציבא's לשון הרע, his kingdom was split, which led to עבודה זרה and exile. Next, רבי יונתן says anyone who claims שלמה sinned is mistaken. The גמרא tests this against פסוקים about his wives, the altars he 'built,' and 'he did evil.' It concludes that שלמה failed to stop his wives, so the פסוק blames him as if he had sinned. Teachings follow about בת פרעה's idolatrous music and about how רומי began at the time of שלמה's marriage and ירבעם's golden calves. רבי יונתן then says יאשיהו never sinned and reads his 'return' as repaying, from his own money, the cases he judged as a boy. רב disagrees and calls יאשיהו the greatest בעל תשובה, and great penitents of later generations are named. The פרק במה בהמה ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: מפיבשת defends himself to דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting מפיבשת's defense: ציבא slandered him, and he leaves the judgment to דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...your servant. And he slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do whatever is good in your eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of the verses where מפיבשת tells דוד that ציבא lied about him. This sets up דוד's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מפיבשת's claim is that ציבא tricked him and then slandered him. He does not argue hard. He praises דוד as being 'like an angel of God' and accepts whatever ruling דוד gives. This is the defense that דוד must now weigh against ציבא's report.

keyTerms.meaning: son of יהונתן, grandson of שאול
servant of שאול's household who accused מפיבשת

phrases.english: your servant. And he slandered your servant
phrases.notes: This amud begins mid-verse (II Samuel 19:27–28).

phrases.english: to my lord the king
but my lord the king is like an angel of God
so do what is good in your eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the verse quotation begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מפיבשת claims ציבא slandered him and leaves the verdict to דוד.

steps.title: דוד splits the field, and מפיבשת replies
steps.stepSummary: דוד rules that מפיבשת and ציבא will divide the field. מפיבשת answers, 'Let him take it all, now that the king has come home in peace.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The king said to him: 'Why keep talking? I have said: you and ציבא will divide the field.' מפיבשת said to the king: 'Let him even take everything, since my lord the king has come home in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next verses: דוד's split ruling and מפיבשת's reply. The גמרא is setting up its own reading of that reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד does not fully restore מפיבשת's property. He gives half to ציבא, which shows he partly believed ציבא's report. מפיבשת's answer sounds generous on the surface, but the גמרא will read hidden bitterness into it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read מפיבשת's reply as simple loyalty. The very next step shows that the גמרא hears it as a complaint.

phrases.english: And the king said to him
why do you speak any more of your matters?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי אַתָּה וְצִיבָא תַּחְלְקוּ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.english: I have said: you and Ziba shall divide the field.
And Mephibosheth said to the king
let him even take everything
since my lord the king has come
in peace to his own house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ לָמָּה תְּדַבֵּר עוֹד דְּבָרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives דוד's response to the defense quoted in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד divides the field between מפיבשת and ציבא.

steps.title: מפיבשת's hidden complaint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains מפיבשת's words: 'I waited for your safe return, and this is how you treat me? My grievance is with the One who brought you back.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מפיבשת said to דוד: 'I kept saying, "When will he come back in peace?" And you do this to me? My complaint is not against you. It is against the One who brought you back in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interprets מפיבשת's reply as a hidden complaint against God for bringing דוד home safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'since the king came home in peace' is read as bitterness, not joy. If you are angry at God for saving דוד, that shows real resentment. So ציבא's report about מפיבשת was not baseless.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading shows that מפיבשת really did harbor resentment. That sets up the name מריב בעל in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי ״מָתַי תָּבֹא בְּשָׁלוֹם״,
phrases.english: He said to him: I was saying, 'When will you come in peace?'
and you do this to me?
It is not against you that I have grievances
but against the One who brought you back in peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי מָתַי תָּבֹא בְּשָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the final verse quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That מפיבשת was resentful, which lends support to ציבא's report.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A close reading of 'אחרי אשר בא אדני המלך בשלום'.

steps.title: The verse calls him מריב בעל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a verse in דברי הימים that calls יהונתן's son מריב בעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'And the son of יהונתן was מריב בעל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a verse that gives מפיבשת a different name, מריב בעל. It is setting up a question about that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'היינו דכתיב' means 'this is what the verse is hinting at.' The גמרא claims that this odd name reflects מפיבשת's quarrel with God.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what is written / this explains the verse

phrases.english: This is what is written: 'And the son of Jonathan was Meriv-Baal,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a verse that supports the reading in step 3.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א ח:לד, 'ובן יהונתן מריב בעל'.

steps.title: But his name was מפיבשת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: was his name really מריב בעל? His name was מפיבשת!
steps.simpleTranslation: Was מריב בעל really his name? His name was מפיבשת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the verse uses a name he was not called by. This question pushes toward an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since his known name is מפיבשת, the different name must be teaching something. The question opens the door to reading the name as a description of what he did.

phrases.english: And was Meriv-Baal his name?
Was his name not Mephibosheth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the name in the verse cited in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The name מריב בעל in the verse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His actual name was מפיבשת, so why does the verse call him something else?

steps.title: He quarreled with his Master
steps.stepSummary: The name means he quarreled with his Master, God. A בת קול called him 'quarrelsome son of a quarrelsome one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because he made a quarrel with his Master, a heavenly voice came out and said to him: 'Quarreler, son of a quarreler.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מריב בעל is a description, not a real name. It means 'one who quarreled with his Master,' and Heaven confirmed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מריבה means quarrel, and בעל means master, here referring to God. His complaint against God for saving דוד earned him this label. The בת קול adds that he was following a family pattern.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה מְרִיבָה עִם בְּעָלָיו.
phrases.english: Rather, because he made a quarrel with his Master,
a heavenly voice emerged and said to him:
Quarreler, son of a quarreler.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁעָשָׂה מְרִיבָה עִם בְּעָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the name is a description of his behavior, not a real name.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מריב בעל seems to be a second proper name.
steps.terutzMaskana: מריב בעל describes מפיבשת's quarrel with God.

steps.title: Explaining 'son of a quarreler': שאול's quarrel
steps.stepSummary: 'Quarreler' refers to what we just said. 'Son of a quarreler' refers to שאול, who 'quarreled in the valley.' רבי מני explains that he argued about the law of the valley, עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Quarreler' means what we just said. 'Son of a quarreler,' as it is written: 'And שאול came to the city of עמלק and quarreled in the valley.' רבי מני said: he quarreled over matters of the valley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each half of the בת קול's words. The second half points back to his grandfather שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וירב (and he fought) is read as 'and he quarreled.' בנחל (in the valley) is read as 'about the valley.' This refers to the עגלה ערופה, which is brought in a valley. שאול argued with God: if one murder needs an atonement, why kill all of עמלק? So מפיבשת followed his family pattern of arguing with God.

keyTerms.meaning: and he quarreled in / about the valley

phrases.english: 'Quarreler': that which we said.
'Son of a quarreler': as it is written:
'And Saul came to the city of Amalek
and quarreled in the valley,'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי: עַל עִסְקֵי נַחַל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said: concerning matters of the valley.
phrases.notes: Refers to the עגלה ערופה, which is done in a valley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two halves of the בת קול in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול, too, quarreled with God, over the command to wipe out עמלק.

steps.title: Split the field, split the kingdom
steps.stepSummary: רב: when דוד split the field, a בת קול declared that רחבעם and ירבעם would split the kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When דוד said to מפיבשת, 'You and ציבא will divide the field,' a heavenly voice came out and said: 'רחבעם and ירבעם will divide the kingdom.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב teaches that Heaven answered דוד's unfair split with a matching punishment: his own kingdom would be split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is מידה כנגד מידה, punishment that matches the act. Dividing the field corresponds to dividing the kingdom. רחבעם, from דוד's line, and ירבעם would later split Israel in two.

keyTerms.meaning: son of שלמה, king of יהודה
first king of the northern kingdom

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
At the time David said to Mephibosheth:
'You and Ziba shall divide the field,'
a heavenly voice emerged and said to him:
'Rehoboam and Jeroboam shall divide the kingdom.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד לִמְפִיבֹשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to דוד's ruling from step 2 and states its consequence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dividing the field led to the division of the kingdom.

steps.title: The terrible cost of accepting slander
steps.stepSummary: רב: had דוד not accepted לשון הרע, the kingdom would not have split, Israel would not have served עבודה זרה, and we would not have been exiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If דוד had not accepted לשון הרע, the kingdom of דוד's house would not have been divided, Israel would not have worshipped idols, and we would not have been exiled from our land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב traces a chain of national disasters back to one act: דוד accepting ציבא's slander.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting the slander led to the split field, which led to the split kingdom. The split kingdom led to ירבעם's golden calves, which led to עבודה זרה. That in turn led to exile. One act of believing לשון הרע set off the whole chain.

keyTerms.meaning: if only / had it not been that

steps.whatToRemember: Accepting לשון הרע, even by someone as great as דוד, can cause huge damage: the divided kingdom, עבודה זרה, and exile.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is a classic source for how serious it is to accept לשון הרע, not only to speak it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אִילְמָלֵי לֹא קִיבֵּל דָּוִד לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
phrases.english: Had David not accepted slander,
the kingdom of the house of David would not have been divided,
and Israel would not have worshipped idols,
and we would not have been exiled from our land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילְמָלֵי לֹא קִיבֵּל דָּוִד לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 8's consequence into the full chain of national disaster.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's accepting לשון הרע caused the split kingdom, עבודה זרה, and exile.

steps.title: Whoever says שלמה sinned is mistaken
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני quotes רבי יונתן: saying שלמה sinned is a mistake. The proof is a פסוק that compares his heart to דוד's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said that רבי יונתן said: Anyone who says שלמה sinned is simply mistaken. The פסוק says, 'His heart was not whole with ה׳ his God like the heart of דוד his father.' That means only this: his heart was not as complete as דוד's. But he did not actually sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic. רבי יונתן says שלמה did not sin, and he brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from reading the פסוק closely. The only complaint the פסוק makes is that שלמה was not on דוד's level. If he had actually sinned, the פסוק would have said so. So the criticism is about his level of perfection, not about a real sin.

keyTerms.meaning: King שלמה, the son of דוד
Like the heart of דוד his father
But he also did not sin

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same pattern we saw with דוד on this daf. The claim is not that שלמה was perfect. It is that his failing was below the level of a real sin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
Anyone who says Solomon sinned
is nothing other than mistaken,
as it says: "And his heart was not whole"

phrases.aramaic: עִם ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו כִּלְבַב דָּוִד אָבִיו״ —
phrases.english: "with ה׳ his God, like the heart of David his father" —

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְבַב דָּוִד אָבִיו הוּא דְּלָא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: like the heart of David his father he was not,
phrases.notes: This is the only failing the פסוק mentions.

phrases.english: but he also did not sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר שְׁלֹמֹה חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new figure in the series of 'he did not really sin' statements, after the discussion of דוד and מפיבשת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה did not sin. He only fell short of דוד's complete devotion.

steps.title: What about the verse that his wives turned his heart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יונתן with a פסוק that seems to say שלמה's wives led him astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק, 'When שלמה was old, his wives turned his heart away'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem. The first half of the same פסוק (מלכים א יא:ד) seems to say outright that שלמה strayed because of his wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his wives 'turned his heart' after other gods, that sounds like a real sin. This directly contradicts רבי יונתן's claim. The question format 'how do I explain' means: this פסוק does not seem to fit your view.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain this (a פסוק that seems to contradict)

phrases.english: But how do I establish (explain)
"And it was at the time of Solomon's old age"
"that his wives turned away his heart" —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from step 10 using another part of the same passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's claim that שלמה did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says his wives turned his heart after other gods, which sounds like a real sin.

steps.title: That verse follows רבי נתן, who noticed the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this פסוק should be read like רבי נתן, who himself noticed that it clashes with 'like the heart of דוד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק follows רבי נתן. רבי נתן pointed out a contradiction within the פסוק. One part says, 'When שלמה was old, his wives turned his heart.' But the other part says, 'like the heart of דוד his father.' That means he was only not on דוד's level, but he also did not sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by sending us to רבי נתן. First it quotes the contradiction רבי נתן raised, which sets up his solution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן had the exact same question: the two phrases seem to clash. Pointing to him shows that רבי יונתן's view is not alone. The real answer, how to reread 'turned his heart,' comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose reading of the פסוק resolves the problem
He raised a contradiction (between two sources)

phrases.english: That follows Rabbi Natan.
For Rabbi Natan raised a contradiction: it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְהִי לְעֵת זִקְנַת שְׁלֹמֹה נָשָׁיו הִטּוּ אֶת לְבָבוֹ״,
phrases.english: "And it was at the time of Solomon's old age that his wives turned away his heart,"
but isn't it written: "like the heart of David his father" —

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְבַב דָּוִד אָבִיו הוּא דְּלָא הֲוָה
phrases.english: like the heart of David his father he was not,
but he also did not sin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 11 by bringing in רבי נתן, who raised the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to an earlier authority's reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His wives turned his heart' means he actually served idols.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי נתן already saw the clash and had a way to reread the פסוק (explained next).

steps.title: They tried to lead him after other gods, but he did not go
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן's solution: the wives pushed him toward other gods, but שלמה did not follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: 'When שלמה was old, his wives turned his heart to go after other gods.' They pushed, but he did not go.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is רבי נתן's actual answer. The wives tried to pull him toward idols, but he never actually went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'to go after other gods' describe what the wives were aiming for, not what שלמה did. So the פסוק describes pressure, not action. That fits 'he did not sin' from step 10.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
"And it was at the time of Solomon's old age"
"that his wives turned away his heart"
"to go after other gods" —
phrases.notes: This was their goal, not his action.

phrases.english: but he did not go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to step 11 with רבי נתן's rereading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק (an attempt, not an act)
steps.terutzMaskana: The wives tried to lead him, but he did not go, so he did not sin.

steps.title: But the verse says שלמה built an altar for כמוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a פסוק says שלמה built a במה for כמוש, the idol of מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'Then שלמה built a במה for כמוש, the abomination of מואב'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge. Another פסוק says שלמה built an altar for an idol, which sounds like a clear sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if he did not 'go after' idols, building an altar for one is an action. That seems to defeat both רבי נתן's reading and רבי יונתן's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: He built (literally a future-tense form, 'he will build')
A raised altar or platform for offerings

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "Then Solomon built a high place (altar)"
"for Kemosh, the abomination of Moab" —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: ״אָז יִבְנֶה שְׁלֹמֹה בָּמָה לִכְמוֹשׁ שִׁקֻּץ מוֹאָב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a stronger challenge after step 13's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שלמה did not sin (and did not follow idols)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Building an altar for כמוש is an actual act of idol worship.

steps.title: He wanted to build it but did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שלמה only wanted to build the altar but never built it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he wanted to build it, but he did not build it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק describes only an intention, not a finished act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יבנה is in the future-tense form ('will build'). The גמרא reads that as a plan that never happened. This is the same move as with the wives: an attempt, not an action.

phrases.english: That he sought to build but did not build.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by reading יבנה as an intention.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the verb form as describing an intention
steps.terutzMaskana: He only wanted to build it.

steps.title: The same word is used for יהושע, who really built
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: יבנה is also used for יהושע's altar, which he clearly built. So with שלמה too, he really built it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, what about the פסוק 'Then יהושע built an altar to ה׳'? Would you say he wanted to build but did not? Rather, he built it. Here too, he built it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last answer. It shows from another פסוק that the word יבנה means a real, finished building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, אז יבנה, describes יהושע's altar, and everyone agrees יהושע really built it. So יבנה cannot mean 'only wanted to build.' That puts the challenge from step 14 back in force: the פסוק does say שלמה built the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, according to your logic (introduces a reductio)
יהושע, who built an altar on הר עיבל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has now concluded that שלמה sinned. It has only rejected one answer, the 'he only wanted to build' reading. The גמרא will still give another explanation of the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method: test a reading of a word by checking the same word elsewhere in תנ״ך. If the reading fails there, it fails here too.

phrases.english: But now (according to this):
"Then Joshua built an altar to ה׳" —
that he sought to build but did not build?!
Rather, he built it,
here too, he built it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה: ״אָז יִבְנֶה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִזְבֵּחַ לַה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 15, which brings back the challenge of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the 'he wanted but did not build' reading of יבנה, not רבי יונתן's overall claim
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same form יבנה describes יהושע's altar, which was really built, so it cannot mean an unfulfilled intention.

steps.title: A new approach: רבי יוסי's ברייתא on the altars near ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the rejected answer and brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי quotes the פסוק about the altars 'that שלמה built.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like the ברייתא: רבי יוסי says: 'And the altars that were in front of ירושלים, to the right of the Mount of Olives, which שלמה king of Israel built for עשתרת, the abomination of the צידונים, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new answer by quoting a ברייתא. Right now it is only setting up the פסוק. The actual explanation comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer, that שלמה only wanted to build, was rejected. So the גמרא brings a פסוק from the story of יאשיה, who destroyed these altars. רבי יוסי will read this פסוק closely to show that 'שלמה built' does not have to mean he literally built them.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The Mount of Olives (literally 'Mount of Anointing,' named for its olive oil; the פסוק in מלכים calls it הר המשחית, 'Mount of Destruction')
Abomination, a word for an idol

phrases.english: Rather, as it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei says:
"And the altars that were before Jerusalem
phrases.notes: מלכים ב כג:יג, part of the story of יאשיה's cleanup

phrases.english: which were on the right of the Mount of Olives
which Solomon king of Israel built
for Ashtoret, the abomination of the Zidonim, etc."
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on to say that יאשיה defiled (destroyed) them

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 16 with a new reading from a ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Non-literal reading of the פסוק (introduced here, completed in Step 19)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שלמה built' means he literally built idol altars
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק will be shown to credit actions to kings who did not literally do them

steps.title: אסא and יהושפט had already destroyed all idolatry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי asks: could it be that the righteous kings אסא and יהושפט left these altars standing until יאשיה came? They destroyed all the idolatry in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible that אסא came and did not destroy them, and יהושפט came and did not destroy them, until יאשיה came and destroyed them? Didn't אסא and יהושפט destroy all the idolatry in ארץ ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יוסי points out that the פסוק cannot be literal. Earlier kings had already wiped out these altars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יאשיה destroyed the altars. But אסא and יהושפט lived before him and cleared out all idolatry. So the altars were already gone, and the claim that יאשיה destroyed them must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? (a word that signals 'this can't be')
A righteous king of יהודה, son of אסא
A later righteous king of יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: This question is aimed at the part about יאשיה, not at שלמה. רבי יוסי first proves the פסוק is not literal about יאשיה, and then uses that to explain the part about שלמה.

phrases.english: Is it possible that Asa came and did not destroy them,
Jehoshaphat came and did not destroy them,
until Josiah came and destroyed them?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: But didn't all the idolatry in the Land of Israel
Asa and Jehoshaphat destroy it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal reading of the פסוק quoted in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal claim that יאשיה destroyed these altars
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Earlier kings had already destroyed all idolatry, so nothing was left for יאשיה to destroy

steps.title: The earlier king is compared to the later king
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links שלמה to יאשיה. יאשיה did not destroy the altars but gets the credit, for praise. שלמה did not build them but gets the blame, for disgrace.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק compares the earlier ones to the later ones. Just as the later ones did not do it, yet the פסוק credits it to them as praise, so too the earlier ones did not do it, yet the פסוק pins it on them as disgrace.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers his own question. The פסוק puts שלמה and יאשיה side by side, and neither one literally did the act it describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיה is praised as if he destroyed the altars because of his great efforts against idolatry. In the same way, שלמה is blamed as if he built them, because he allowed his wives' idolatry to happen. This answers Step 14: שלמה did not build the altars, but the פסוק blames him for them.
steps.whatToRemember: A פסוק can credit someone with an act they did not literally do, either to praise them or to blame them. שלמה did not build the altars. He is blamed because he let it happen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key that resolves the challenge from Step 14 and protects the opening claim that שלמה did not actually sin.

phrases.english: Rather, it compares the earlier ones to the later ones:
just as the later ones did not do it
and it attributed it to them for praise,
so too the earlier ones did not do it
and it attributed it to them for disgrace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of Step 18 and so answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: הקש comparing two kings: credit or blame given without literal action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe literal actions, so יאשיה destroyed and שלמה built
steps.terutzMaskana: Neither king literally acted. יאשיה is credited for praise and שלמה is blamed for disgrace

steps.title: But the פסוק says שלמה did evil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: a פסוק openly says 'שלמה did evil in the eyes of ה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And שלמה did evil in the eyes of ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק that seems to clearly say שלמה sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the altars were only blamed on him, this פסוק says outright that שלמה himself did evil. That seems to go against the claim that he did not sin.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
Evil in the eyes of ה׳

phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And Solomon did evil in the eyes of the Lord"!
phrases.notes: מלכים א יא:ו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge after the altar problem was solved
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שלמה did not sin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק directly says שלמה did evil

steps.title: He failed to stop his wives
steps.stepSummary: Because שלמה should have protested against his wives' idolatry and did not, the פסוק treats him as if he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because he should have protested against his wives and did not, the פסוק counts it against him as if he sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'did evil' means failing to stop his wives, not doing idolatry himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה's fault was being passive. He had the power to stop his wives and did not use it. The פסוק describes this failure as strongly as if he had sinned himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק counts it against him

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who could stop a wrong and does not is held responsible as if he did it himself.

phrases.english: Rather, because he should have
protested against his wives and did not protest,
the verse counts it against him as if he sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לִמְחוֹת בְּנָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: 'did evil' means failing to protest
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמה failed to stop his wives, and the פסוק treats this as if he sinned

steps.title: Better to be a servant for idolatry than to have 'he did evil' written
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: it would have been better for that צדיק to be a servant for idolatry than to have 'he did evil' written about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It would have been better for that צדיק to be a servant for 'something else' (idolatry), and not have it written about him, 'And he did evil in the eyes of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a closing thought about how serious this label is for שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שלמה did not truly sin, being called 'he did evil' in a פסוק (מלכים א יא:ו) is a terrible disgrace. שמואל says doing low labor for idolatry, like chopping wood or drawing water, would have been easier for him than this permanent label.

keyTerms.meaning: It would be better for him
'Something else,' a polite name for idolatry

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: שלמה did not sin, but his failure to stop his wives earned him a written label that was worse for him than doing hard labor for idolatry.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It would have been better for that righteous man
to be a servant for 'another thing' (idolatry),

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יִכָּתֵב בּוֹ ״וַיַּעַשׂ הָרָע בְּעֵינֵי ה׳״.
phrases.english: and not have written about him: "And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: נוֹחַ לוֹ לְאוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a statement on how serious the label from Step 21 is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being labeled 'he did evil' is worse for a צדיק than doing menial labor for idolatry

steps.title: בת פרעה brought idolatrous music, and שלמה did not protest
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל describes what שלמה failed to protest. בת פרעה brought him a thousand kinds of musical instruments. She explained which songs were used for which idol, and he said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: When שלמה married בת פרעה, she brought him a thousand kinds of musical instruments. She told him, 'This is how we serve this idol, and this is how we serve that idol.' He did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a concrete picture of the failure to protest that was mentioned in step 21. It shows what שלמה should have stopped and did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said in general terms that שלמה should have protested. This מימרא supplies the real-life scene behind that claim. שלמה himself did not serve idols, but he stayed silent while idolatry was described and practiced in his own home.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of פרעה, one of שלמה's foreign wives
kinds of music or musical instruments

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה,
phrases.english: When Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter,
she brought to him a thousand kinds of musical instruments,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרָה לוֹ כָּךְ עוֹשִׂין לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פְּלוֹנִית,
phrases.english: and she said to him: This is what we do for this idol,
and this is what we do for that idol,
and he did not protest against her.
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase. It connects back to the idea that failing to protest counts as sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the failure to protest that was the basis for blaming שלמה in steps 21 and 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמה stayed silent while בת פרעה brought idolatrous music into his home and explained it to him.

steps.title: At שלמה's marriage, the foundation of רומי was planted
steps.stepSummary: Also in the name of שמואל: when שלמה married בת פרעה, the angel גבריאל planted a reed in the sea. A sandbar formed around it, and the great city of רומי was later built on that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: When שלמה married בת פרעה, גבריאל came down and stuck a reed into the sea. A sandbar built up around it, and on it the great city of רומי was built.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same speaker shows the long-term damage of that marriage. The empire that would one day punish Israel began at that very moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step showed the sin itself, which was silence. This step shows its consequence. רומי, which later destroyed the בית המקדש, is pictured as being 'planted' on the day of the marriage, waiting to be used as the tool of punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: a sandbar, a build-up of mud and sand

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנָּשָׂא שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה
phrases.english: When Solomon married Pharaoh's daughter,
Gabriel descended and stuck a reed into the sea,
and a sandbar grew up around it,
and upon it the great city of Rome was built.
phrases.notes: רומי is the empire that would later destroy the second בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sin of silence to its historical consequence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beginnings of רומי, the future destroyer of Israel, came about at the moment שלמה married בת פרעה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: Italy began when ירבעם set up the golden calves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a parallel tradition. On the day ירבעם set up two golden calves, one in בית אל and one in דן, the first hut was built in the place that became Italy.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: On the day ירבעם brought in two golden calves, one in בית אל and one in דן, a single hut was built. That was the beginning of Italy of Greece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a similar idea. It ties the start of the Roman world to a different sin, the golden calves of ירבעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tradition places the first settlement of Italy at a later date and links it to the open idolatry of ירבעם. The two traditions fit together: the land formed in שלמה's time, and the first building went up in ירבעם's time. Either way, each major sin added another layer to the empire that would punish Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
Italy of Greece, meaning the Greek-influenced region of Italy

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
On that very day that Jeroboam brought in
two golden calves,
one in Beth-El and one in Dan,
a single hut was built,
and that is Italy of Greece.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁהִכְנִיס יָרָבְעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel tradition to step 24, linking the rise of רומי to the sin of ירבעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first building of Italy went up on the day ירבעם set up the golden calves.
steps.whatToRemember: The sins of Israel's kings, first שלמה's silence and then ירבעם's calves, are pictured as the starting points of the empire that would later destroy ירושלים.

steps.title: Anyone who says יאשיהו sinned is mistaken
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן opens a new topic. Anyone who claims יאשיהו sinned is simply wrong, because the פסוק says he did what was right and followed all the ways of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Anyone who says יאשיהו sinned is just mistaken. The פסוק says, 'He did what was right in the eyes of ה׳ and walked in all the ways of דוד his father.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new section in the series of 'anyone who says so-and-so sinned is mistaken.' This time the subject is יאשיהו, and a פסוק is brought as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier statements about other righteous figures, this מימרא defends יאשיהו's record. The proof is the פסוק saying he walked in 'all' the ways of דוד, which leaves no room for a period of sin.

keyTerms.meaning: what is right in the eyes of ה׳
the way of דוד his ancestor

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:
Anyone who says that Josiah sinned
is nothing other than mistaken,
as it is stated: "And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord,
and he walked in all the way of David his father."
phrases.notes: The word 'all' is the heart of the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ חָטָא אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, יאשיהו, in the series of defenses of righteous figures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יאשיהו did not sin, as the פסוק says he walked in all the ways of דוד.

steps.title: But the verse says יאשיהו 'returned,' which suggests he once sinned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יונתן's claim. Another פסוק says no king before יאשיהו 'returned' to ה׳ like he did. Returning seems to mean he first sinned and later did תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how do I explain the פסוק: 'And like him there was no king before him who returned' to ה׳...?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the previous statement and sets up the next move. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שב' (returned) usually means doing תשובה after a sin. If יאשיהו 'returned,' that seems to show he once sinned, which contradicts רבי יונתן. The גמרא will need to explain what he 'returned' from.

keyTerms.meaning: how do I explain (this other source)?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as the final word that יאשיהו sinned. It is only a question, and the answer, coming next, will keep רבי יונתן's position.

phrases.english: However, how do I establish the meaning of
"And like him there was no king before him
who returned, etc."?
phrases.notes: 'Returned' suggests he once did wrong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 26 using a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונתן's claim that יאשיהו never sinned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes יאשיהו as one who 'returned' to ה׳. Returning implies an earlier sin, which contradicts the claim that he never sinned.

steps.title: יאשיהו returned money from the cases he judged as a youth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge. יאשיהו's 'returning' means he paid back the money in every case he judged from age 8 to 18.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every case that he judged from age eight until age eighteen, he gave the money back to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 27. The 'returning' in the פסוק was not תשובה for a sin. It was returning money from court cases he judged as a young king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'returning' must mean coming back after sinning. The answer reads 'returning' more literally, as giving money back. יאשיהו became king at eight. He worried that as a boy he may have judged wrongly, so he repaid the people he had ruled against. That way, רבי יונתן's claim that יאשיהו never sinned still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He returned them (gave the money back)

phrases.english: For every case that he judged
phrases.notes: This continues from the challenge. It explains what 'returned' in the פסוק really means.

phrases.english: from age eight until eighteen
phrases.notes: יאשיהו was crowned at eight (מלכים ב כב:א). The big turning point came in his eighteenth year.

phrases.english: he returned them to them
phrases.notes: He paid back the people he had ruled against.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכָּל דִּין שֶׁדָּן מִבֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה עַד שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה הֶחְזִירָן לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Returned' (שָׁב) implies he first sinned and later did תשובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Returned' means he gave back money from cases he may have misjudged as a youth. No sin is implied.

steps.title: He paid from his own money, as the verse says 'with all his might'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible misunderstanding. The money did not come from the other side of the case. יאשיהו paid it himself, as hinted by בכל מאדו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you will say that he took from this one and gave to that one? The verse says 'with all his might' (מאדו, his money). This teaches that he gave them from his own money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its answer. A reader might think יאשיהו just took the money back from the winner and gave it to the loser. The פסוק shows he paid it out of his own pocket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he had only moved money from one side to the other, he could have caused a new wrong if his first ruling was actually correct. The word מאדו is read as 'his money,' just as it is in קריאת שמע. So the פסוק itself says his 'return' was done with his own money.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps you will say (raising a possible mistake in order to reject it)
His 'might,' read here as his money

steps.confusionAlert: מאדו here does not mean physical strength. Just as in ובכל מאדך of קריאת שמע, it is read as 'with all your money.'

phrases.english: Lest you say
phrases.notes: The גמרא brings up a mistaken reading so it can reject it.

phrases.english: he took from this one and gave to that one
phrases.notes: Meaning: he took the money back from the winner and handed it to the loser.

phrases.english: the verse states: 'with all his might'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב כג:כה

phrases.english: that he gave them from his own
phrases.notes: He paid with his own money.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר נָטַל מִזֶּה וְנָתַן לָזֶה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the answer of Step 28 with a proof from the פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarification supported by a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He simply moved the money back from the winning side to the losing side.
steps.terutzMaskana: He paid them out of his own money (בכל מאדו).

steps.title: רב disagrees: יאשיהו was the greatest penitent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יונתן's view argues with רב. רב says יאשיהו was the greatest בעל תשובה of his generation, and there is one such person in רב's own generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב, for רב said: There is no one greater among penitents than יאשיהו in his generation, and one in our generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another אמורא, רב, holds the opposite view. רב says יאשיהו did sin and did real תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling יאשיהו the greatest בעל תשובה means he had something to repent for. That clashes with רבי יונתן, who said anyone who claims יאשיהו sinned is mistaken. רב also mentions a great penitent in his own generation, which sets up the next question.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav,
phrases.notes: רבי יונתן's view argues with רב.

phrases.english: as Rav said:
there is no one greater among penitents
than Josiah in his generation
and one in our generation.
phrases.notes: There is also one great penitent in רב's own time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to the position just defended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, יאשיהו sinned and did תשובה. He was the greatest בעל תשובה of his generation.

steps.title: Who is the penitent of רב's generation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who רב meant by 'one in our generation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question. Who was the great penitent in רב's time? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב mentioned a person without naming him. This question is not a challenge. It just asks for the identity of that person.

phrases.english: And who is he?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the person רב mentioned
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name of the great בעל תשובה in רב's generation

steps.title: It was אבא, or his brother אחא
steps.stepSummary: The answer is אבא, father of רבי ירמיה בר אבא. Some say it was אחא, his brother. The two were known to be brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was אבא, the father of רבי ירמיה בר אבא. Some say it was אחא, the brother of אבא, the father of רב ירמיה בר אבא. As the Master said: רבי אבא and אחא were brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the penitent. It gives two versions of who it was, and it adds a source showing the two men were brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions point to the same family. The line דאמר מר simply confirms that אבא and אחא were brothers, so the second version makes sense. It does not settle which version is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting a known statement)

phrases.english: Abba, the father
of Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba.
And some say: Acha, the brother
of Abba, the father
of Rav Yirmeya bar Abba.
As the Master said:
Rabbi Abba and Acha were brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבא, father of רבי ירמיה בר אבא. Or, by another version, his brother אחא.

steps.title: רב יוסף adds another penitent in his generation
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says there is one more great בעל תשובה in his own generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: And there is another one in our generation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds to רב's list. He says his generation also had a great penitent. This sets up the question of who it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף lived later than רב. So 'our generation' here means a different, later time. He is adding a new name, not arguing with רב.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
And another one in our generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף וְעוֹד אֶחָד בְּדוֹרֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further example to רב's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was also a great בעל תשובה in רב יוסף's generation.

steps.title: Who is רב יוסף's penitent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who רב יוסף was referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is he?
steps.whatsHappening: Again, the גמרא asks a simple identity question. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question has the same form as Step 31. It asks for a name and does not challenge anything.

phrases.english: And who is he?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the person רב יוסף mentioned
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The name of the great בעל תשובה in רב יוסף's generation

steps.title: It was עוקבן בר נחמיה, known as נתן דצוציתא
steps.stepSummary: The penitent was עוקבן בר נחמיה ריש גלותא, who is the same person known as נתן דצוציתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: עוקבן בר נחמיה, the ריש גלותא. And this is the one called נתן דצוציתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רב יוסף's penitent. It adds that he is the same man known by the nickname נתן דצוציתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא connects two names for one person. עוקבן was his name, and נתן דצוציתא was the nickname he was known by. Sefaria explains צוציתא as sparks or rays that came from his head.

keyTerms.meaning: Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in בבל
And this is the same as
Sparks or rays (part of his nickname)

phrases.english: Okvan bar Nechemya
the Exilarch.
And that is 'Natan detzutzita.'
phrases.notes: The same man is known by this nickname.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עוקבן בר נחמיה ריש גלותא, also known as נתן דצוציתא

steps.title: רב יוסף's dream showed his repentance was accepted
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells of a dream he had while dozing at a lecture. In it, he saw a hand stretched out to receive נתן דצוציתא, showing that his תשובה was accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I was sitting at the פירקא (public lecture) and I was dozing. I saw in a dream that he stretched out his hand and received him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף supports his claim with a personal experience. In a dream, he saw נתן דצוציתא being welcomed, which showed his תשובה was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 said this man was a great בעל תשובה. This dream gives support for that claim. Being 'received' with an outstretched hand shows Heaven accepted his תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: A public lecture (often given on a יום טוב or שבת)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on יאשיהו. רבי יונתן says he never sinned, and his 'return' was paying back money from his youthful rulings with his own funds. רב says he was the greatest בעל תשובה of his generation. True תשובה is accepted, as the examples of later penitents show.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I was sitting at the lecture,
and I was dozing,
and I saw in a dream
that he stretched out his hand and received him.
phrases.notes: Sefaria understands that an angel received נתן דצוציתא, a sign his תשובה was accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא בְּפִירְקָא וַהֲוָה קָא מְנַמְנַמְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim that נתן דצוציתא was a great בעל תשובה
steps.raayaObject: That נתן דצוציתא's תשובה was real and accepted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's dream of him being received

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter of במה בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the fifth פרק of מסכת שבת, במה בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, במה בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק. It marks that the chapter במה בהמה is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is not part of the argument. It expresses a promise to come back and review this chapter. The next פרק begins after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
The name of the fifth פרק of שבת: 'With what may an animal go out'

phrases.english: We will return to you, Bameh Behemah

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the entire פרק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק of במה בהמה is complete.
